To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incidence of myocardial infarctions in young individuals is increasing, even in populations least susceptible to coronary artery disease.
smoking is the major risk factor for AMI in young population.

(i) AMI in young patients is a rising problem in rural/semi-urbsn areas; (ii) the incidence of AMI is more in young males than females; (iii) smoking is the most common risk factors for AMI in young population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the profile of young AMI patients in a rural/ semi-urban population.
the study of the profile of young patients (below the age of 40 years) with acute myocardial infarcation in a semi-urban population.
the epidemiology of AMI in a rural/semirural population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence of AMI is on the rise even in young individuals and the risk of mortality is less than in their counterparts of older age group.
young age is not protective against AMI in the Indian scenario.
young individuals with AMI in our population have different profile than those reported in developed countries and hence, need to be studied further.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMI in young patients is on the rise and needs immediate attention
the profile of AMI in our young population is different from the older ones.
smoking cessation and early reporting to hospital would help in reducing morbidity and mortality in these young patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the young patients with chest pain need to be investigated and treated with the same zeal as the older age group, since they are equally prone to complications.
even in a population where AMI is not very common, young individuals are not spared from its clutches and hence need to be targeted for prevention of this disease.
the young patients of AMI are not only at the mercy of the risk factors but also the socio-economic factors.
